message:
test(host): ask both links whether they are still answering

Test 1. Built, not run -- it needs a host, which the reviewer runs.

The two-dispatcher test asserted that both sides were answered and that neither paid the other's
deadline. It never asked the question the whole task is about: are the control links still alive
while a preview is stuck? On 2026-09-15 they were not. Sessions connected, listed windows, drew a
picker, and went silent, because the dispatcher was inside PrintWindow and never got back to
reading. That was measured for one dispatcher in 049d588 and nowhere for two.

The two links are checked differently because they are different things. TCP is a strict
request/response stream, so it cannot be pinged while its own thumbnail request is outstanding; it
is pinged immediately after, and what matters is that the answer comes at once rather than after
another deadline. The UDP session runs its own control loop, so the evidence there is the round
trip it completed WHILE the TCP request was in flight, plus a loop still running and a session
still connected at the end, with nothing having reported session-dead or control-lost.

The reviewer asked for this and was right to: without it their live run would confirm the timing
and say nothing about the thing that actually broke.

Still opt-in, still SKIP by default, still starts nothing -- verified after building: zero
GNLinkStream processes.
